items.context: D1=B (full Go subpackages) is now settled. Each subpackaged domain needs a stable import path. Options follow common Go conventions; the choice affects every import line in the new code and any future tooling that walks the API tree.

options.label: `api/domain/<name>` (e.g., `api/domain/ai`, `api/domain/billing`)
options.rationale: Most explicit — `domain/` directory itself screams architecture. Easy to grep for 'all domains', easy to enumerate. Matches the proposed-action wording in notes.md ('api/domain/{landing,billing,...}').

options.label: `api/<name>` directly (e.g., `api/ai`, `api/billing`)
options.rationale: Shorter import paths, flatter tree. But mixes domain dirs with `api/main.go` and other top-level files, making the screaming-architecture intent slightly less obvious.

options.label: `api/internal/<name>` (e.g., `api/internal/ai`)
options.rationale: Uses Go's `internal/` to enforce that nothing outside `api/` can import these subpackages. Strongest encapsulation; useful if anything outside `api/` ever tries to reach in. Less idiomatic for a scenario where the API package is itself the boundary.

items.context: Per your D1 note, if subpackaging all 8 domains is too much for one execution, pick a few and defer the rest. The Server struct shows that some domains have minimal shared-helper dependencies (likely acyclic when extracted) while others touch session/rate-limit/email helpers heavily. Recommendation: subpackage the 4 most isolated first; defer the 4 that share more helpers.

options.label: Subpackage 4 isolated domains: `ai`, `remote-profile`, `user-auth`, `metrics` — defer `billing`, `downloads`, `admin`, `landing`
options.rationale: These four touch the fewest shared helpers (AI has its own `AIGatewayDeps`; remote-profile is a single service; user-auth owns its rate limiter + session; metrics is read-mostly). High confidence of acyclic extraction. Leaves billing (touches Stripe + plans + payment settings + credits), downloads (3 services + authorizer), admin (cross-cutting), and landing (uses landing-config + assets + SEO + variant) for a follow-up where shared helpers can be designed deliberately.

options.label: Subpackage all 8 domains in this execution
options.rationale: Maximum value in one go; matches the screaming-architecture intent fully. Risk: shared helpers (rate limiter, session manager, email service) will likely force mid-execution package extractions, ballooning the diff and increasing chance of behavior drift. Reasonable only if cycles do not appear.

options.label: Subpackage 1-2 domains as a pilot (`ai` + `remote-profile`), defer the rest
options.rationale: Lowest-risk pilot to validate the subpackage convention end-to-end before scaling. Smallest diff, but leaves most of the value on the table; requires multiple follow-ups.

items.context: When a domain extraction triggers an import cycle (e.g., subpackaged `billing` and subpackaged `admin` both need `RateLimiter`, which currently lives in the flat `api` package), the agent needs a pre-agreed rule. Mid-execution package design (creating a new `api/shared/` or `api/platform/` package on the fly) is risky for behavior preservation; deferring the offending domain is safer but slower.

options.label: On cycle: revert that domain's move and add it to the deferred list. Do not extract new shared packages mid-execution.
options.rationale: Highest behavior-preservation guarantee. Keeps the diff focused. The follow-up backlog item gets to design `api/shared/` deliberately with its own plan + review.

options.label: On cycle: extract a minimal `api/shared/<helper>/` subpackage in the same execution and continue.
options.rationale: Avoids deferring more domains; finishes more of the refactor now. But each shared-package extraction is itself a behavior-sensitive change (helper init order, package-level state) that deserves its own review.

options.label: On cycle: keep the helper in the flat `api` package and have subpackages import upward via interfaces declared in the subpackage.
options.rationale: Consumer-defined interfaces break the cycle without moving the helper. Idiomatic Go but adds an interface-shim layer per shared dependency; can obscure which concrete helper is in use.

items.context: Whatever subset is deferred from D2 needs a follow-up. Granularity affects scheduling and review cost: one item bundles all deferred work (one PR, one review, one test pass) but is bigger; per-domain items parallelize but multiply ceremony.

options.label: Single follow-up `execute` item covering all deferred domains, inheriting acceptance_allow
options.rationale: Lowest backlog overhead. The follow-up plan can sequence domains itself. Matches your D1 note phrasing ('a new backlog item or items'). Best when the deferred set is 2-4 domains.

options.label: One follow-up item per deferred domain
options.rationale: Maximum parallelism — multiple agents could pick different domains. But each item needs its own workshop pass, and shared-helper decisions get duplicated/contradicted across items.

options.label: Group deferred work under a new initiative with per-domain members
options.rationale: Best if the deferred set is large (5+) or if shared-helper design needs its own dedicated item alongside the per-domain moves. Heavier to set up; overkill for the recommended D2=A subset of 4.

Added a new Phase 6 for the follow-up backlog item, a 'Settled Decisions' section that captures your D1 override verbatim, and a transitional callout requirement for ARCHITECTURE.md so mixed subpackage/legacy state is not silently confusing.
